newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end above 19,000,gains capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end above 19,000,gains capped.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended above the 19,000 points barrier on Thursday for the first time since January 6, but dealers said further gains were likely to be limited and slow.

They said the buying spree was triggered largely by a newspaper report that said the Japanese government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan companies and other troubled financial firms.
The market largely ignored the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract added 455 points to close at 19,060 after hitting a high of 19,120. Turnover was a healthy 25,185 lots.
"People had been worried about the financial sector with all the bad news and banks being downgraded," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
The report of possible government land purchases in Thursday's Nihon Keizai Shimbun provided the first spot of positive news in a while, he said.

He said the market seemed to ignore a subsequent Reuters report quoting a Finance Ministry official as saying the government was not considering allocating new public funds to buy collateralised land now held by loan-collecting bodies.
"People didn't bother with that. They just wanted buy above 18,800," he said. "You just couldn't sell today. If you did, you'd get hurt," he added.
But he said further gains were likely to be capped around the 19,500 region. "The charts show that we could be going into overbought territory so the market momentum will slow down."
He said the March Nikkei was likely to undergo a correction on Friday but strong support would emerge at 18,800 and 18,650.
Taiwan stock index futures ended near their day highs after falling early in line with Taipei stocks on news of Deng's death.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract settled at 322.9 against its opening 32.0 on volume of 524 lots.
